analysis:
Examined SSDPrefixCache.swift BASE lines 657–1836 and the complete changed hunk. The sole change replaces one removalLock-protected retirement operation with removeInSlices, acquiring the lock and checking hasSafeRoot/ownsEvictionRoot separately for each slice (HEAD 1794–1800). This introduces interleaving between retirement slices; no concrete security regression is established by the supplied evidence.
Relevant T-041/A-001/TB-007 protections in the surrounding BASE source include salt-scoped HMAC block and window identities (862–920, 1183), donation benefit/staging/endurance gates, authenticated weight/layout/tag bindings and bounded streaming reads (1382–1409, 1627–1663), cancellation fallback, shared staging reservations and ticket cleanup (1341–1373, 1499–1570, 1722–1753). Those paths are unchanged. No supplied change affects serving authorization, attestation, wire encryption, credentials, billing or privileged-helper authority.
Integration must inspect SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.removeInSlices and its changed callers: verify nil handling stops or safely skips work after ownership/root invalidation, aggregate externalChange/indexedBytesFreed/removed correctly, and preserve file/index consistency when writes, eviction or destructive changes interleave between slices. SSDPrefixCache still reconciles external removals after the aggregate result, while evictOldestEntry relies on its externalChange and byte accounting (BASE 1777–1784). The helper implementation is absent from this batch, so these PR-specific contracts remain unresolved rather than findings.
